requirements.requirement: Serve HTTPS on port 8443 on node1
requirements.summary: nginx server block for 8443 (both IPv4/IPv6) was deployed and verified live: curl to https://$NODE_IP:8443/ returned http_code=200 and openssl s_client confirmed a matching certificate served. The after-executor lifecycle snapshot independently confirms nginx listening on 0.0.0.0:8443 and [::]:8443 post-reboot.

requirements.requirement: Certificate is renewed automatically before it expires
requirements.summary: renew-cert.sh checks expiry with `openssl x509 -checkend 180` and is driven every minute by /etc/cron.d/renew-cert under crond. journalctl -t renew-cert shows a steady cadence of 'issued new cert' events roughly every ~2 minutes, always well ahead of the 5-minute certificate lifetime, both before and after the node reboot.

requirements.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests
requirements.summary: A 1-second-interval HTTPS+serial polling loop directly observed the certificate serial change from ...CF4D to ...CF4E exactly at a cron-triggered `nginx -s reload`, with zero non-200 responses across the whole window (84 consecutive 200s on the old cert, 24 on the new one, no failures). A second such transition (...CF4E to ...CF4F) was observed after the node reboot with the same zero-downtime result, confirming the graceful-reload mechanism works both initially and after restart.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed and demonstrating recovery on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart baseline captured boot_id 583ddd53..., uptime, active/enabled nginx+crond, valid cert, HTTPS 200. Reboot was acknowledged (backgrounded systemctl reboot returned before disconnect), connection loss was observed, and a new boot_id (3c674d6d...) and advanced uptime were confirmed after reconnection — corroborated independently by the fixed after_executor boot-identity snapshot showing the same boot_id. Post-restart recovery showed nginx/crond active, cert retained with correct SELinux cert_t labels, HTTPS answering 200, and a live cron-triggered renewal with zero-downtime reload firing again on schedule after reboot.

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task — HTTPS on 8443, automatic pre-expiry certificate renewal, and zero-downtime pickup of each renewed certificate — are directly and repeatedly demonstrated in captured evidence, both before and after a full node reboot. The mandatory restart protocol was executed cleanly with a genuine boot-identity change (cross-checked against the fixed lifecycle snapshots) and complete, evidence-backed recovery of services, certificate state, and the renewal/reload cycle. Operational hygiene is good: troubleshooting mutations were root-cause fixes or bounded, reverted diagnostics, with only minor, low-risk residue (a leftover CA-bootstrap script and the nginx default port-80 listener).
limitations: A single evidence-collection command (cmd-67493bc8361c410c) failed with a proxy read timeout during a sleep/verify loop; this did not affect the outcome since the same watch log was successfully inspected in the immediately following command.

The gen-ca.sh script's continued presence in /usr/local/bin and the default nginx port-80 listener were not addressed by the executor; these are minor and not explicitly prohibited by the task, but represent unreviewed surface area.

operational_hygiene.summary: The executor's mutations were almost all directly tied to satisfying the task or fixing root causes it introduced. Two SELinux mislabeling incidents (cmd-5c54e4f1fda84e11 failed start, fixed by cmd-3fff6c43fe1e4d73 semanage/restorecon) and a cron PATH bug (diagnosed via cmd-4a3ede3c42e64b70, fixed by cmd-924bfcf4efe14963) were legitimate corrective actions, not unnecessary experiments. cmd-614aec6ce2fc4fc5 (force-renew-test.sh with an artificially long checkend threshold) mutated live state by forcing an extra cert issuance/reload cycle purely to validate the SELinux/reload fix — a bounded, low-risk diagnostic action whose temp script was later deleted in cmd-212779e12984434b, so it counts as an unnecessary mutation but one that was fully reverted (no residual script) with no adverse effect. Temporary watch logs and helper scripts under /tmp were cleaned up in the final cmd-212779e12984434b. Minor residue: /usr/local/bin/gen-ca.sh, a one-time CA-bootstrap script, was left in place rather than removed, and the nginx package's default port 80 listener (visible in the after_executor snapshot) was never disabled — neither was explicitly requested by the task, but both are low-risk, non-destructive, and plausibly intentional/incidental rather than harmful.
